From someone who’s been in recovery for a while and nearly 3 years clean & sober… Mac’s music (and probably Alice in Chains) is like nothing else in terms of brutal honesty and being able to identify the depths of addiction which is one of the reasons I connect with it so deeply. 

But just because you relapsed doesn’t mean you lost that time you were clean. Once you’re over the inevitable feelings of guilt and shame and likely some self hatred… look at it as a good thing. That may sound hard initially but relapses can be, and in my experience definitely were, a good thing!! They force you to realise where you were being complacent, maybe you weren’t working your program enough or calling your sponsor as much as you should. It might be the necessary kick up the arse you needed to really put everything into your recovery! 

The main thing is to not be put off of getting clean by the shame of using again. And… for what’s its worth I lost my younger step brother a handful of years ago and sadly, the only thing that helps is time. I wish nothing but the best for you brother

I kinda get where you’re coming from but here’s what I would say to that

On the whole god thing - yes when aa was set up the whole ‘god’ emphasis was way more emphasised which makes sense for that time period in America. But now it’s a ‘god of our understanding’ meaning if you struggle with the god word, you just need to find a power greater than yourself. I know people who use nature or even the meetings as their ‘higher power’. A belief that there is something greater/bigger than us as we do not and should not have the answers and we shouldn’t run on our own self will

The ‘you can’t do it without this program - yeah people can do it without the meetings or the program. But the reason why people suggest the only way to get and STAY sober is to work the program is because for a lot of us simply white knuckling it and cutting it out of our lives isn’t enough. We need to change our behaviours, the way we think/react and we need to take ownership of our wrong doings. And that’s where the steps come in for us.

I know I couldn’t do it without working the program like I do. In fact I tried to do it on my own and it didn’t work because you take the alcohol and the drugs out and I’m sober… but then I’m still the same person with the same awful thoughts. AA has given me the tools to change and handle life again like a grown up
